perspective:
From Keith Ndiaye’s available perspective:

- Keith works at a construction company; Elizabeth is the receptionist there. They are friendly, professional colleagues, often interacting when Keith handles paperwork or project updates.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth had been unusually curt/short with him over several days. He wondered whether he had unknowingly upset her through a misunderstanding or mistake.
- Keith asked Elizabeth directly. She told him she was not upset with him; she was dealing with personal stuff and apologized if she seemed short.
- Keith felt sympathetic and offered to listen or take a coffee break. Elizabeth accepted, saying it was kind and that coffee sounded good.
- During the coffee break, Elizabeth shared more about her personal stresses. Keith perceived them as quite severe.
- Keith suggested Elizabeth consider talking to a professional, saying an external perspective can sometimes help.
- Elizabeth told him she had thought about it but was not sure and felt hesitant about seeking help.
- Keith noticed Elizabeth became slightly withdrawn afterward. He worried he might have overstepped or embarrassed her and said so. Elizabeth told him he did not overstep, she appreciated his concern, and it was just a lot to think about.
- Later, Keith observed Elizabeth seeming more open and appreciative. She thanked him, said it meant a lot, and that she felt better knowing she had his support.
- Keith believes Elizabeth values his support and feels more comfortable around him. He intends to maintain a supportive relationship and remain available for chats or breaks.
